title: Common Applications & MS Office
subtitle: AXIS 2026 section: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, browsers, shortcut keys & command prompt — about 12 exam questions

readingSections.title: The MS Office Section: What to Expect
readingSections.quickSummary: About 12 questions, Medium-Hard: MS Office ~5Q, browsers ~2Q, shortcut keys ~2Q, command prompt ~2Q, key workflows ~1Q. No negative marking.
content: Common Applications and MS Office is the first sub-section of the AXIS Technical Assessment - roughly 12 of the 45 shared questions. Published breakdowns weight it as: MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) about 5 questions, browser fundamentals about 2, shortcut keys about 2, command prompt about 2, and key workflows about 1.

The questions are pure product knowledge: shortcut keys, file formats, view names, formula results, mail-field meanings. They reward people who have actually used Office - every fact below is a published-PYQ or standard-document fact.
Because the timer is shared (45 minutes for all 45 technical questions), this section should take you under 8 minutes - it is the fastest scoring area once the tables in this topic are memorised.

subsections.title: Question style
subsections.content:
Three recurring styles:
1. Shortcut recall - 'Which shortcut underlines selected text?' (Ctrl+U).
2. Feature/result recall - 'What does =AVERAGE(5,10,15) return?' (10) or 'Which view shows bulleted points?' (Outline).
3. Concept recall - 'What is the CC field for?' (awareness recipients) or 'What is the blank space outside the print area?' (margin).

subsections.title: Preparation strategy
subsections.content: Memorise the shortcut tables (they cover 4-5 questions alone), then the one-line definitions (margin, CC, hyperlink, outline view). Practice reading formula questions slowly: AVERAGE, CONCATENATE and range syntax (B8:B10) have all appeared verbatim.

quickRevision: 12 questions: Office ~5, browsers ~2, shortcuts ~2, command prompt ~2, workflows ~1.
Shortcut tables are the highest-density marks in the whole Technical Assessment.
No negative marking - answer everything.
Target under 8 minutes for this sub-section.
tricks: Ctrl+letter shortcuts are identical across Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook for the universal set (N/O/S/P/W/Z/Y) - learn once, answer four applications' questions.
Excel formula questions: mentally evaluate the innermost function first, then read options.
Outlook calendar shortcuts follow Ctrl+Shift+initial: A for Appointment, Q for meeting (Q after 'schedule'), K for tasK.
Command prompt questions in PYQs love cd navigation - cd .. goes up one level, cd../.. goes up two.
patterns: 'Which shortcut key...' - answer is almost always a Ctrl combo from the tables.
'What is the result of the formula...' - evaluate the function; watch text vs number results.
'Which view shows...' - Word: Outline (bulleted), Print Layout (default), Web Layout, Draft.
'The blank space outside the printing area' - margin.

pyqPatterns.question: What is the result of =CONCATENATE("Good", " ", "Morning")?
pyqPatterns.approach: CONCATENATE joins arguments verbatim: Good + space + Morning = 'Good Morning'.

pyqPatterns.source: TalentBattle Accenture MS Office PYQ set
pyqPatterns.question: While using formulas in Excel, the notation B8:B10 indicates:
pyqPatterns.approach: All cells from B8 to B10 inclusive - the colon is a RANGE operator, not multiplication.

readingSections.title: MS Word & PowerPoint Essentials
readingSections.quickSummary: Word: four views, formatting shortcuts, margins. PowerPoint: five views, Ctrl+M inserts a slide, F5 starts the show, hyperlinks jump between slides.
content: MS Word questions test views, formatting and page setup. The four Word views: Print Layout (default, shows page boundaries), Web Layout (browser-like), Outline (document as bulleted heading structure - a published PYQ), and Draft (plain text, no images). Margins are the blank space outside the printing area - another verbatim PYQ.

Formatting shortcuts follow a logic: Ctrl+B/I/U for bold/italic/underline; Ctrl+L/E/R/J align left/centre/right/justify; Ctrl+= subscript; Ctrl+Shift+= superscript; Ctrl+1/Ctrl+2 single/double line spacing.

PowerPoint questions test views and show control. Views: Normal (editing), Slide Sorter (thumbnails - reorder here), Reading, Slide Show. Ctrl+M inserts a NEW SLIDE (published PYQ). F5 starts the slideshow from the beginning; Shift+F5 from the current slide; Esc ends it. Hyperlinks navigate between slides within or across presentations - another verbatim PYQ.

subsections.title: Word views table
subsections.content:
Print Layout - default; page boundaries, headers, margins visible.
Web Layout - no page breaks; browser-like flow.
Outline - headings as bulleted structure; reorganise by dragging.
Draft - text only; hides images and page furniture for fast editing.

subsections.title: Word formatting shortcuts
subsections.content:
Ctrl+B bold | Ctrl+I italic | Ctrl+U underline
Ctrl+L / Ctrl+E / Ctrl+R / Ctrl+J - align left / centre / right / justify
Ctrl+= subscript | Ctrl+Shift+= superscript
Ctrl+1 single spacing | Ctrl+2 double spacing
Shift+Tab outdents a list level (published PYQ); Tab indents.

subsections.title: PowerPoint control table
subsections.content:
Ctrl+M - insert new slide
F5 - show from beginning; Shift+F5 - from current slide; Esc - end show
Slide Sorter view - drag to reorder thumbnails
Hyperlink (Ctrl+K) - jump to another slide, file or web page
B key - black screen during show; W - white screen

quickRevision: Word views: Print Layout (default), Web, Outline (bulleted), Draft.
Ctrl+E centres; Ctrl+U underlines; Ctrl+= subscript; Ctrl+Shift+= superscript.
Margin = blank space outside the printing area.
Ctrl+M = new slide; F5 = show from start; Esc = end show; hyperlinks jump slides.
tricks: Alignment shortcut letters spell their direction: L-eft, E-centEr, R-ight, J-ustify.
Subscript vs superscript: plain Ctrl+= pushes DOWN (sub), adding Shift pushes UP (super).
Outline view question: the phrase 'bulleted points' or 'heading structure' in the stem is the giveaway.
PowerPoint 'insert new slide' is Ctrl+M - M for 'make slide', not Ctrl+N (new presentation).
patterns: 'Shows the contents as bulleted points' - Outline view.
'Blank space outside the printing area' - margin (header/footer live inside margins' edges).
'Move this line one level to the left' - Shift+Tab (outdent).
'Navigate from one slide to another within or across presentations' - Hyperlink.

pyqPatterns.question: In MS PowerPoint, the shortcut Ctrl+M helps the user to:
pyqPatterns.approach: Insert a new slide. Ctrl+N would create a whole new presentation.

pyqPatterns.question: Which Word view shows the document's contents as bulleted points?
pyqPatterns.approach: Outline view - it renders the heading hierarchy as bullets.

pyqPatterns.question: Cursor is before 'I' in 'Introduction' - which option moves the line one level LEFT?
pyqPatterns.approach: Shift+Tab outdents; plain Tab indents; Alt+Tab switches windows.

readingSections.companyNote: Word views + PowerPoint Ctrl+M are repeat PYQs - both appeared in published Accenture practice sets.

readingSections.title: MS Excel Essentials
readingSections.quickSummary: Formulas start with '='; B8:B10 is a range; AVERAGE/SUM/COUNT/MAX evaluate to single values; Ctrl+PgUp switches worksheets.
content: Every Excel formula begins with '=' - a published PYQ asks exactly this (options: @, =, &, #). After the equals sign come function names, cell references and operators. The colon is the RANGE operator: B8:B10 means ALL cells from B8 through B10 inclusive - another verbatim PYQ.

Core functions returning single values: SUM adds, AVERAGE divides the sum by the count, COUNT counts NUMERIC cells only (text is ignored), MAX/MIN pick extremes, CONCATENATE glues text arguments verbatim.
Worksheet navigation: Ctrl+PgUp moves to the PREVIOUS worksheet and Ctrl+PgDn to the next - a published PYQ. Ctrl+Home jumps to A1; F2 edits the active cell.

subsections.title: Formula evaluation - worked PYQs
subsections.content:
=AVERAGE(5, 10, 15) -> (5+10+15)/3 = 10 (published PYQ).
=CONCATENATE("Good", " ", "Morning") -> 'Good Morning' (space argument included verbatim - published PYQ).
=SUM(2, 3) -> 5.  =MAX(4, 9, 2) -> 9.
=COUNT(1, 2, "abc") -> 2 - text is not counted.

subsections.title: References and ranges
subsections.content:
B8 - one cell.  B8:B10 - the range B8 to B10 (published PYQ: 'all cells from B8 to B10').
B8,D10 - a UNION of two cells (comma).  $B$8 - absolute reference (does not shift on copy).
A1 vs R1C1 - the two reference styles; A1 is default.

subsections.title: Navigation and structure
subsections.content:
Ctrl+PgUp / Ctrl+PgDn - previous / next worksheet (published PYQ).
Ctrl+Home - cell A1.  Ctrl+End - last used cell.  F2 - edit cell.
A worksheet is a grid of 1,048,576 rows x 16,384 columns (XFD); a workbook holds many worksheets saved as one .xlsx file.

quickRevision: Formulas start with '='. Range operator is ':' (B8:B10 = B8 through B10).
AVERAGE = sum/count; COUNT ignores text; CONCATENATE joins verbatim.
Ctrl+PgUp = previous sheet; Ctrl+PgDn = next sheet.
Ctrl+Home = A1; F2 = edit cell.
tricks: Evaluate function questions arithmetically on paper - AVERAGE(5,10,15) is (5+10+15)/3, not the middle value.
CONCATENATE includes EVERY argument exactly as typed - count the quote-wrapped spaces.
COUNT vs COUNTA: COUNT = numbers only; COUNTA = all non-empty cells. PYQ options love this swap.
Worksheet-switch questions: PgUp goes BACK (previous), PgDn goes FORWARD (next).
patterns: 'What should come before the formula?' - '=' (published PYQ; distractors @, &, #).
'B8:B10 indicates...' - all cells B8 to B10 (published PYQ; distractor: product of B8 and B10).
'Shortcut to move to the previous worksheet' - Ctrl+PgUp (published PYQ).

pyqPatterns.question: When working on an MS Excel sheet, to enter a formula in a cell, what should come before the formula?
pyqPatterns.approach: The equals sign '=' - options typically offer @, =, &, #.

readingSections.companyNote: Excel formula-evaluation questions appeared verbatim in published Accenture sets - practise reading them slowly rather than pattern-matching.

readingSections.title: Outlook, Email & Browser Essentials
readingSections.quickSummary: Outlook: Ctrl+Shift+A/Q/K for appointment/meeting/task; deleted mail lands in Trash/Deleted Items. Email: CC informs, BCC hides. Browser: Ctrl+W closes a tab.
content: Outlook organises work into Mail, Calendar, Tasks, Contacts and Notes. The calendar shortcuts follow Ctrl+Shift+initial: Ctrl+Shift+A creates an APPOINTMENT, Ctrl+Shift+Q schedules a MEETING (from any folder), Ctrl+Shift+K creates a TASK - all three are syllabus-listed facts.

Email fields: To = primary recipients who must act; CC (carbon copy) = recipients kept AWARE but not expected to act (published PYQ); BCC (blind carbon copy) = hidden recipients invisible to everyone else. A mail deleted by accident lands in Trash / Deleted Items - another published PYQ.

Browser basics: Ctrl+W closes the current TAB (published PYQ; Ctrl+T OPENS one), Ctrl+T new tab, Ctrl+Shift+T reopens a closed tab, Ctrl+D bookmarks, F5 refreshes, Ctrl+H history. A URL's domain identifies the site; HTTPS means TLS-encrypted transport.

subsections.title: Outlook calendar & task shortcuts
subsections.content:
Ctrl+Shift+A - new Appointment (Calendar folder, or right-click a time block)
Ctrl+Shift+Q - new Meeting request (works from any folder)
Ctrl+Shift+K - new Task
Ctrl+N - new item (context-dependent: mail, appointment, contact, task)
Ctrl+O - open selected item

subsections.title: Mail fields decoded
subsections.content:
To - must read/act.
CC (carbon copy) - awareness only, visible to all (published PYQ: 'include recipients who should be aware but don't need to act').
BCC (blind carbon copy) - hidden from other recipients; protects privacy on mass mails.
Subject + attachment etiquette: meaningful subject, files attached not embedded.

subsections.title: Folder and browser facts
subsections.content:
Deleted mail -> Trash / Deleted Items folder (published PYQ; options: Draft, Spam, Inbox).
Draft = unsent mail being written; Spam/Junk = filtered suspicious mail.
Browser: Ctrl+W close tab (published PYQ), Ctrl+T new tab, Ctrl+D bookmark, Ctrl+H history, F5 reload.
Ctrl+P prints - universal across Office and browsers.

quickRevision: Outlook: Ctrl+Shift+A appointment, Ctrl+Shift+Q meeting, Ctrl+Shift+K task.
CC = aware-but-no-action; BCC = hidden recipients.
Deleted mail -> Trash/Deleted Items.
Ctrl+W closes a browser tab; Ctrl+T opens one.
tricks: Outlook calendar trio = Ctrl+Shift + first letter of the OUTCOME: Appointment, meeting(Q), tasK - memorise Q and K as the odd two.
CC vs BCC: the B is 'blind' - BCC recipients are invisible to everyone.
Tab questions: W = close (Window), T = open (Tab).
Deleted-mail questions: Trash is the safety net; Draft never held the mail.
patterns: 'Recipients who should be aware but need not act' - CC.
'Accidentally deleted mail is saved in which folder?' - Trash/Deleted Items.
'Close a tab on a browser' - Ctrl+W (published PYQ; distractors Ctrl+T/A/X).
'Schedule a meeting from any folder' - Ctrl+Shift+Q.

pyqPatterns.question: If by accident a mail is deleted, which folder saves it?
pyqPatterns.approach: Trash (Deleted Items). Draft holds unsent drafts, Spam holds filtered mail.

pyqPatterns.question: Purpose of the CC field in email?
pyqPatterns.approach: Include recipients who should be aware of the message but don't need to act.

pyqPatterns.question: Which of the following can close a tab on a browser?
pyqPatterns.approach: Ctrl+W. Ctrl+T opens a new tab; Ctrl+A selects all; Ctrl+X cuts.

readingSections.companyNote: The Outlook Ctrl+Shift trio and the CC/BCC definitions are syllabus-listed verbatim - free marks if memorised.

readingSections.title: Universal Shortcuts & Command Prompt Basics
readingSections.quickSummary: One universal Ctrl set spans all Office apps; command prompt PYQs test cd navigation, ipconfig and file commands.
content: The universal Windows/Office shortcut set is identical across Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and most Windows programs: Ctrl+N new, Ctrl+O open, Ctrl+S save, F12 save as, Ctrl+P print, Ctrl+W close, Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Y redo, Ctrl+C copy, Ctrl+X cut, Ctrl+V paste, Ctrl+A select all, Ctrl+F find. Learning this one table answers shortcut questions for four applications at once.

Command prompt carries about 2 questions per published breakdown. Navigation: cd changes directory, cd .. up one level, cd../.. (or cd ..\..) up TWO levels - a published PYQ asked exactly this with mixed-slash distractors. dir lists contents; cls clears screen.

Network commands: ipconfig shows the machine's IP configuration; ping tests reachability of a host; tracert traces the route packets take. File operations: copy, move, del (delete), mkdir (make directory).

subsections.title: The universal table (learn once, answer everywhere)
subsections.content:
Ctrl+N new | Ctrl+O open | Ctrl+S save | F12 save as
Ctrl+P print | Ctrl+W close | Ctrl+Z undo | Ctrl+Y redo
Ctrl+C copy | Ctrl+X cut | Ctrl+V paste | Ctrl+A select all
Ctrl+F find | Ctrl+B bold | Ctrl+I italic | Ctrl+U underline
Ctrl+Home start of document | Ctrl+End end of document

subsections.title: Command prompt navigation
subsections.content:
cd folder - enter folder; cd .. - up one level; cd../.. - up two levels (published PYQ answer; distractors mixed \ and /).
dir - list directory contents.  cls - clear screen.  exit - close prompt.
Drives: C:, D: switch drives; paths use \ (backslash) in Windows.

subsections.title: Network & file commands
subsections.content:
ipconfig - show IP configuration (ipconfig /all for details).
ping host - test reachability and latency.
tracert host - hop-by-hop route.
copy, move, del file - file operations; mkdir/rmdir - make/remove directory.

quickRevision: Universal set: N O S P W Z Y + C X V A F - one table, all apps.
cd .. = up one; cd../.. = up two; dir = list; cls = clear.
ipconfig = my IP config; ping = reachable?; tracert = route.
F12 = Save As (not Ctrl+Shift+S).
tricks: Shortcut questions with identical options across apps: pick from the universal table - Office apps share it.
cd PYQ: two levels up = cd../.. - the distractor with backslashes (cd..\..) is the trap; the published answer used forward slashes.
ipconfig vs ping: ipconfig SHOWS your config; ping TESTS another host. Stems asking 'show my IP' -> ipconfig.
Undo/Redo pair: Z back, Y forward - works in every Office app.
patterns: 'Which command takes you two steps backward from any directory?' - cd../.. (published PYQ).
'Shortcut to save' - Ctrl+S; 'Save As' - F12.
'Show IP configuration' - ipconfig.
'Which key held down while selecting a word/phrase in Word?' - Shift (published PYQ).

pyqPatterns.question: Which command takes you two steps backward from any particular directory?
pyqPatterns.approach: cd../.. - each .. climbs one level; the mixed-backslash distractor is wrong for the published answer.

pyqPatterns.question: Which key is held down to select a word or phrase in MS Word?
pyqPatterns.approach: Shift - hold Shift and arrow/click to extend the selection.

readingSections.companyNote: Command prompt carries ~2 questions per published breakdown - the cd-navigation PYQ alone has appeared in multiple Accenture sets.

formulas.title: The Universal Ctrl Table (All Office Apps)

formula.text: New, Open, Save, Print, Close, Undo, Redo, Copy, Cut, Paste, Select-all, Find - identical across Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook.

formulas.whenToUse: Any 'which shortcut does X' question about basic file/edit operations.
explanation: File row: N new, O open, S save, F12 save-as, P print, W close.
Edit row: Z undo, Y redo, C copy, X cut, V paste, A select all, F find.
These bindings predate Office and are shared by virtually every Windows program.
Excel adds navigation on top: Ctrl+PgUp/PgDn switch worksheets.

example.prompt: Which shortcut saves the current document in Word, Excel AND Outlook alike?
steps: The universal save shortcut is Ctrl+S.

formulas.memoryTip: NO SPoWZY: New Open Save Print close Undo Redo + CXVAF.
formulas.commonMistake: Answering F12 for plain 'save' - F12 is Save As.

formulas.title: Word Formatting Shortcut Map

formula.text: Bold-Italic-Underline, align Left-centEr-Right-Justify, subscript/superscript on the = key.

formulas.whenToUse: Formatting shortcut questions in Word (and mostly PowerPoint too).
explanation: Ctrl+B bold, Ctrl+I italic, Ctrl+U underline.
Ctrl+L left, Ctrl+E centre, Ctrl+R right, Ctrl+J justify - E is the only non-obvious one (centEr).
Ctrl+= subscript; Ctrl+Shift+= superscript - same key, Shift flips direction.
Ctrl+1 / Ctrl+2 single / double line spacing; Shift+Tab outdents list levels.

example.prompt: Which shortcut centre-aligns the selected text?

formulas.commonMistake: Ctrl+J for centre - J is justify; centre is Ctrl+E.

formulas.title: Excel Formula Grammar

formula.text: Formulas start with '='; the colon builds an inclusive range; functions return single values.

formulas.whenToUse: Every 'result of the formula' or 'what does this notation mean' Excel question.
explanation: Start every formula with '=' (published PYQ: options @, =, &, #).
B8:B10 = all cells from B8 to B10 inclusive; comma = union of separate cells.
SUM adds; AVERAGE = sum/count; COUNT counts NUMERIC cells only; MAX/MIN extremes; CONCATENATE joins text verbatim.
$B$8 = absolute reference - does not shift when copied.

steps: 5 and 7 are numeric -> 2; the text and empty string are ignored.

formulas.memoryTip: = starts it, : spans it, COUNT skips text.
formulas.commonMistake: Reading B8:B10 as 'product of B8 and B10' - a published PYQ distractor.

formulas.title: PowerPoint Views & Show Control

formula.text: Ctrl+M inserts a slide, F5 starts the show, Esc ends it, Ctrl+K inserts a hyperlink.

explanation: Ctrl+M = insert NEW SLIDE (Ctrl+N would create a whole new presentation).
F5 show from beginning; Shift+F5 from current slide; Esc end; B black / W white screen during show.
Views: Normal (edit), Slide Sorter (reorder thumbnails), Reading, Slide Show.
Hyperlink (Ctrl+K) navigates between slides in the same or another presentation.

example.prompt: Which shortcut inserts a new slide?
steps: Ctrl+M inserts a slide; Ctrl+N opens a new presentation.

formulas.memoryTip: M = 'more slide'. F5 fires the show.
formulas.commonMistake: Ctrl+N for a new slide - that opens a new PRESENTATION.

formulas.title: Outlook Calendar & Mail Field Rules

formula.text: Outlook calendar shortcuts are Ctrl+Shift plus the initial of the outcome; CC informs, BCC hides.

explanation: Ctrl+Shift+A - new Appointment (Calendar folder).
Ctrl+Shift+Q - new Meeting request from ANY folder.
Ctrl+Shift+K - new Task.
To = act; CC = aware but no action needed (visible); BCC = hidden from all recipients.
Deleted mail lands in Trash / Deleted Items; Drafts hold unsent compositions.

example.prompt: Which shortcut schedules a meeting request from any folder?
steps: Meeting = the Q shortcut (works anywhere in Outlook).

formulas.memoryTip: A-Q-K: Appointment, meeting(Q), tasK - only Q and K need memorising.
formulas.commonMistake: CC for hidden recipients - hidden is BCC's job.

formulas.title: Command Prompt Essentials

formula.text: Navigation: cd moves, .. climbs, dir lists; network: ipconfig shows, ping tests.

formulas.whenToUse: Command prompt questions - about 2 per published AXIS breakdown.
explanation: cd folder enters; cd .. up one level; cd../.. up two levels (published PYQ).
dir lists contents; cls clears the screen; exit closes the prompt.
ipconfig shows YOUR IP configuration; ping tests ANOTHER host's reachability; tracert shows the route.
copy/move/del handle files; mkdir/rmdir make/remove directories.

example.prompt: Which command shows your machine's IP configuration?
steps: 'Show MY config' points at the configuration display tool.
ipconfig (ping tests others, it doesn't show yours).

formulas.memoryTip: Two dots = one floor up. ipconfig = mine, ping = theirs.
formulas.commonMistake: ping for 'show my IP' - ping probes remote hosts.

universal-shortcuts.q: Which shortcut OPENS an existing file?
s: O = Open; N = New; S = save; F12 = Save As.

universal-shortcuts.q: Ctrl+W does what in any Office app or browser?

s: X looks like scissors - cut removes and holds on clipboard.
N = New - context decides what kind.

universal-shortcuts.q: Ctrl+Home in Word moves the cursor to:

s: B = Bold; I = italic; U = underline.
R = Right; E = cEntEr; J = Justify.

word-format-shortcuts.q: Which shortcut JUSTIFIES text (flush both sides)?

s: Ctrl+= drops text below the line.
Shift variant raises text above the line.
Ctrl+1 single, Ctrl+2 double, Ctrl+5 = 1.5 lines.

word-format-shortcuts.q: To OUTDENT a bullet one level:
s: Shift+Tab moves left; Tab indents right.

word-format-shortcuts.q: Which shortcut moves one whole WORD right?
Selecting from cursor to line START uses:
s: Shift extends selection; Home = line start; Ctrl+Home = document start.
E is the only non-obvious alignment letter - cEntEr.

excel-formula-syntax.q: Which operator builds an inclusive cell range?

s: Range operator spans everything between the endpoints inclusive.
Arguments join verbatim: Sun + day = Sunday.
Dollar signs = absolute reference - frozen on copy.

ppt-show-control.q: Which shortcut inserts a NEW SLIDE?
s: Ctrl+M = new slide; Ctrl+N = new presentation.
F5 from start; Shift+F5 from current.

ppt-show-control.q: Slide Sorter view is used to:
Pressing B during a show gives a:
Which view is PowerPoint's default editing view?
s: Normal = edit one slide with notes pane.

ppt-show-control.q: Notes for the presenter are typed in:
s: Notes pane sits under the slide in Normal view; visible to presenter only.

ppt-show-control.q: Which key ends the slideshow AND is universal for closing dialogs?

outlook-workflows.q: Ctrl+Shift+A in Outlook creates a new:
s: A = Appointment (Calendar folder or right-click a time block).
Syllabus: 'from any folder in Outlook press Ctrl+Shift+Q'.

outlook-workflows.q: The To field holds recipients who:

s: B = blind - invisible to everyone else.
Drafts hold compositions; Trash holds deleted mail.

outlook-workflows.q: Mail flagged as suspicious lands in:

s: Ctrl+N respects the folder you're in.

outlook-workflows.q: Which folder is the safety net for accidentally deleted mail?
s: Published PYQ: deleted mail is recoverable from Trash/Deleted Items.
dir = directory listing; del deletes files.
ping probes a REMOTE host; ipconfig shows yours.

opts: The hop-by-hop route to a host
s: tracert = trace route, hop by hop.
command-prompt-essentials.a: The hop-by-hop route to a host

command-prompt-essentials.q: Which command makes a new directory?

s: Windows = backslash; URLs use forward slash - the PYQ distractor swaps them.

mcqs.q: Which shortcut saves the current document in Word, Excel and PowerPoint alike?
exp: Ctrl+S = save across every Office app.
F12 is Save As; Ctrl+P prints; Ctrl+N creates a new file.

mcqs.q: Which key opens the 'Save As' dialog?
exp: F12 = Save As in Word, Excel and PowerPoint.

mcqs.q: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y perform:
exp: Z steps BACK (undo), Y steps FORWARD (redo) - universal in Office.

mcqs.q: Which shortcut copies the selection?
exp: C = Copy (original stays), X = Cut (original removed), V = Paste.

mcqs.q: In MS Word, which shortcut UNDERLINES the selected text?
exp: B = Bold, I = Italic, U = Underline - the formatting trio.

mcqs.q: Which shortcut CENTRE-aligns the selected text in Word?
exp: Ctrl+E = cEntEr; L = left, R = right, J = justify.

mcqs.q: Which shortcut applies SUBSCRIPT formatting in Word?
exp: Ctrl+= pushes text DOWN (subscript); adding Shift (Ctrl+Shift+=) raises it (superscript).

mcqs.q: Which shortcut applies SUPERSCRIPT formatting?
exp: Same = key as subscript but with Shift: Ctrl+Shift+= raises the text.

mcqs.q: Which MS Word view shows the document's contents as bulleted points (heading structure)?
exp: Outline view renders headings as a bulleted structure you can drag to reorganise.
Print Layout is the default page view.

mcqs.q: The blank space outside the printing area on a page is called:
exp: Margins frame the printable area; headers/footers live inside the page, at its edges.

mcqs.q: Which key held down lets you SELECT a word or phrase with the mouse/arrows in Word?
exp: Shift EXTENDS the selection from the anchor point; Ctrl selects whole words per click.

mcqs.q: In MS PowerPoint, Ctrl+M:
exp: Ctrl+M inserts a NEW SLIDE.
Ctrl+N would open a whole new presentation.

mcqs.q: Which key starts a slideshow from the BEGINNING in PowerPoint?
exp: F5 = show from the start; Shift+F5 = from the current slide; Esc ends it.

mcqs.q: Which feature navigates from one slide to another slide in the same or another presentation?
exp: Hyperlinks (Ctrl+K) jump between slides within or across presentations.

mcqs.q: To enter a formula in an Excel cell, what must come FIRST?
exp: Every Excel formula starts with '='.
@ heads structured references in tables, not basic formulas.

mcqs.q: In Excel, the notation B8:B10 indicates:
opts: All cells from B8 to B10
The product of B8 and B10
exp: The colon is the RANGE operator: every cell B8 through B10 inclusive.
The 'product' option is the classic distractor.

mcqs.q: What does =AVERAGE(5, 10, 15) return?
What does =CONCATENATE("Good", " ", "Morning") return?
exp: CONCATENATE joins arguments verbatim: 'Good' + ' ' + 'Morning' = 'Good Morning' - the middle space argument matters.

mcqs.q: Which shortcut moves to the PREVIOUS worksheet in Excel?
exp: Ctrl+PgUp = previous sheet; Ctrl+PgDn = next sheet.

mcqs.q: The CC field in an email is used to:
opts: Include recipients who should be aware but need not act
exp: CC (carbon copy) = visibility without action expectation.
Hiding recipients is BCC's job.

mcqs.q: A mail deleted by accident is recoverable from which folder?
exp: Deleted mail lands in Trash / Deleted Items.
Draft holds unsent compositions; Spam holds filtered mail.

mcqs.q: Which shortcut closes a browser TAB?
exp: Ctrl+W closes the current tab; Ctrl+T OPENS a new tab.

mcqs.q: Which command shows your computer's IP configuration?
exp: ipconfig displays the local IP setup; ping TESTS another host.

mcqs.q: Which command lists the contents of the current directory?
exp: dir lists; cls clears the screen; cd changes directory.

mcqs.q: Ctrl+Shift+= (with Shift) applies:
exp: Ctrl+= is subscript; the Shift variant Ctrl+Shift+= is superscript - same key, opposite direction.

mcqs.q: Cursor is before 'I' in the line 'Introduction'. Which option moves this line ONE LEVEL LEFT?
exp: Shift+Tab OUTDENTS (left); plain Tab indents right; Alt+Tab switches applications.

mcqs.q: Ctrl+1 and Ctrl+2 control:
exp: Ctrl+1 = single spacing; Ctrl+2 = double spacing; Ctrl+5 = 1.5 lines.

mcqs.q: Which Word view is the DEFAULT editing view showing page boundaries?
exp: Print Layout is default - it shows pages, margins, headers exactly as printed.

mcqs.q: Which Word view hides images and page furniture for fast text editing?
exp: Draft strips down to text for speed.
Outline shows the heading structure.

mcqs.q: In PowerPoint, which view shows slide THUMBNAILS for easy reordering?
exp: Slide Sorter lays out all slides as thumbnails - drag to reorder.

mcqs.q: Shift+F5 in PowerPoint:
opts: Starts the show from the beginning
Starts the show from the CURRENT slide
exp: F5 = from beginning; Shift+F5 = from the slide you're on.

mcqs.q: During a slideshow, pressing B shows:
exp: B blanks to BLACK; W blanks to WHITE - handy for pauses.

mcqs.q: =SUM(2, 3, "5") in Excel returns:
exp: SUM ignores text arguments: 2+3 = 5. Text like "5" is not coerced by SUM.

mcqs.q: =COUNT(1, 2, "abc", 4) returns:
exp: COUNT counts NUMERIC values only: 1, 2 and 4 -> 3; "abc" is skipped.

mcqs.q: =MAX(4, 9, 2) returns:
exp: MAX returns the largest argument: 9.

mcqs.q: $B$8 in Excel is:
opts: An absolute reference that does not shift when copied
exp: Dollar signs lock the column AND row - absolute reference.

mcqs.q: Ctrl+Home in Excel jumps to:
exp: Ctrl+Home = A1; Ctrl+End = last used cell.

mcqs.q: In Outlook, Ctrl+Shift+A creates a new:
exp: Ctrl+Shift+A = Appointment (Calendar folder; or right-click a time block).

mcqs.q: In Outlook, Ctrl+Shift+K creates a new:
exp: Ctrl+Shift+K = tasK - the K mnemonic.

mcqs.q: In Outlook, Ctrl+Shift+Q (works from any folder) creates a:
exp: Ctrl+Shift+Q schedules a meeting from ANY folder - the syllabus' exact phrasing.

mcqs.q: BCC recipients are:
exp: Blind carbon copy hides the BCC list from everyone - privacy for mass mails.

mcqs.q: Ctrl+Shift+T in a browser:
exp: Ctrl+Shift+T resurrects the last closed tab - a lifesaver after Ctrl+W.

mcqs.q: Ctrl+D in a browser:
exp: Ctrl+D bookmarks the current page; Ctrl+J opens downloads.

mcqs.q: Which command moves UP TWO directory levels in the command prompt?
exp: Each '..' climbs one level; two climbs = cd../.. - the published PYQ answer.

mcqs.q: Which command tests whether another host is reachable?
exp: ping probes a remote host for reachability/latency; ipconfig only shows YOUR config.

mcqs.q: Which command shows the hop-by-hop route to a host?
exp: tracert traces each router hop; ping only confirms arrival.

mcqs.q: Which command DELETES a file from the command prompt?
exp: del (erase) removes files; rmdir removes directories.

mcqs.q: Starting with Microsoft Office 2003, Photo Editor was renamed to:
exp: Office 2003 renamed Photo Editor to Microsoft Office Picture Manager - a trivia PYQ.

mcqs.q: Which is Microsoft Works' relationship to the Microsoft Office suite?
opts: It is a core part of Office
It is NOT part of the Office suite
exp: Microsoft Works was a separate consumer suite - never a component of Office.

mcqs.q: A feature of MS Office that saves the document automatically after certain intervals is:
exp: AutoSave/AutoRecover periodically saves work - the published answer keys this feature against FrontPage/Explorer distractors.

mcqs.q: Which Excel formula returns 'GoodMorning' (no space)?
exp: Dropping the space argument glues the words: 'GoodMorning'.
Option C is invalid - text literals need quotes.

mcqs.q: =AVERAGE(10, 20, 30, 40) equals:
Which shortcut JUMPS between slide shows as a live hyperlink target (insert hyperlink dialog)?
exp: Ctrl+K inserts the hyperlink that navigates between slides/files/web - the published PYQ's 'Hyperlink' feature.

mcqs.q: In Excel, =CONCATENATE("A","-","B") returns:
exp: Arguments join verbatim including the "-" literal: A-B.

mcqs.q: Which pair of Word shortcuts moves one WHOLE WORD left/right?
exp: Ctrl+arrows hop word-by-word; Shift+arrows select character-by-character.

mcqs.q: Which statement about Office file extensions is CORRECT?
exp: Modern (Open XML) formats: .docx / .xlsx / .pptx - legacy were .doc/.xls/.ppt.

mcqs.q: A colleague must REVIEW but never EDIT; another hidden reviewer must stay invisible. Which field pair?
opts: To for reviewer, BCC for hidden
CC for reviewer, CC for hidden
BCC for reviewer, To for hidden
exp: Reviewer-awareness = CC/To; invisibility = BCC - only option A pairs them correctly.

mcqs.q: Which command-prompt sequence lists contents, then clears the screen?
exp: dir lists; cls clears - order matters for the stated sequence.

mcqs.q: Which Excel shortcut EDITS the active cell in place?
exp: F2 enters edit mode at the cell; F4 toggles absolute references; F12 = Save As.

mcqs.q: Which Outlook shortcut pair is CORRECT?
exp: A = Appointment, Q = meeting, K = tasK - option B alone matches.
